title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Perioperative Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibition in Cardiac Surgery Patients: An Open-Label Randomized Pilot Study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Zuurbier CJ; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
study_design: Single-center, open-label randomized pilot sub-study (MERCURI)
setting: Amsterdam University Medical Center; elective cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted adult cardiac surgery; ICU postoperative monitoring
analysis_population: Intention-to-treat (all 55 randomized participants from MERCURI trial included)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted cardiac surgery (mostly valve repair/replacement or combined with CABG)
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily
exposure_timing: Administered from 3 days preoperatively until 2 days postoperatively
follow_up: Hemodynamic and fluid outcomes assessed during the first 24 postoperative hours; other postoperative observations reported without quantified time horizon
funding: European Union Horizon 2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No. 101024833
conflicts_of_interest: One author (D.H.v.R.) reports consultancy/honoraria and research funding from Boehringer Ingelheim, Lilly, Merck, Sanofi, AstraZeneca; honoraria paid to employer. Others report no conflicts.
extraction_notes: This sub-study focuses on hemodynamics, fluids, vasoactive support, AF, and CK-MB. Prespecified review outcomes (AKI, mortality, heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA, length of stay) were not quantitatively reported here; AKI findings were primarily reported in the parent MERCURI publication cited as ref. 11.
overall_extraction_notes: No analysis-ready data were reported for the prespecified outcomes (postoperative AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA, or length of hospital stay). The paper states in the Conclusion that SGLT2 inhibition was not associated with increased risk of AKI, hypotension, or arrhythmias, but provides no quantitative data or definitions suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore, outcome fields are left empty per protocol.

title: Dapagliflozin for inpatient hyperglycemia in cardiac surgery patients with type 2 diabetes: randomised controlled trial (Dapa-Hospital trial).
authors: Kuchay MS; Khatana P; Mishra M; Surendran P; Kaur P; Wasir JS; Gill HK; Singh A; Jain R; Kohli C; Bakshi G; Radhika V; Saheer S; Singh MK; Mishra SK
study_design: Investigator-initiated, prospective, open-label, randomized controlled trial (treat-to-target), intention-to-treat analysis
setting: Single tertiary care center (Medanta The Medicity Hospital, Gurugram) — hospitalized adult cardiac surgery patients (postoperative) with T2D
analysis_population: All randomized participants analyzed by intention-to-treat (n=250)
surgery_or_procedure: Cardiac surgery (coronary artery bypass grafting, valvular heart surgery, or combination)
intervention_or_exposure: Dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily added to basal–bolus insulin regimen
exposure_timing: Initiated on the day of transition from IV insulin to subcutaneous insulin (day 2 post-surgery); early postoperative inpatient period
follow_up: In-hospital period up to 12 days post-randomization; creatinine measured at baseline and days 1, 2, 4, 6
funding: Investigator-initiated; grant support from the Diabetes and Endocrinology Foundation (DEF), India
conflicts_of_interest: Some authors reported speaker honoraria/relationships with pharmaceutical companies; the article states no other conflicts relevant to this work.
overall_extraction_notes: Mortality, postoperative heart failure, and composite MACE were not explicitly reported; thus not extracted.

title: Empagliflozin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing On-Pump CABG: The POST-CABGDM Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Pitta FG; Lima EG; Tavares CAM; Martins EB; Rached FH; Moreira EM; Mioto BM; Lottenberg SA; Bolta PMP; Justino LG; Favarato D; Carvalho LNS; Pinesi HT; Barbosa CTM; Dallan LAO; Dallan LRP; Barbosa MHM; Kalil Filho R; de Lemos JA; Serrano CV
study_design: Single-center, investigator-initiated, pragmatic, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome adjudication (modified intention-to-treat analysis)
setting: Instituto do Coração, Hospital das Clínicas, University of São Paulo; tertiary academic hospital; single-center elective on-pump CABG program
analysis_population: Modified intention-to-treat: all randomized patients who underwent surgery (n=145; 71 empagliflozin, 74 control)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), planned on-pump; 9 procedures were performed off-pump due to intraoperative decisions
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 25 mg orally once daily plus standard care for at least 3 months prior to CABG; discontinued 72 hours before surgery
exposure_timing: Preoperative initiation ≥3 months before surgery; drug stopped 72 h pre-op
follow_up: Primary AKI assessed within 7 days post-surgery; secondary and safety outcomes assessed during hospitalization and up to 30 days after surgery
funding: No external funding; supported by resources from the Atherosclerosis Unit, Instituto do Coração, Hospital das Clínicas HCFMUSP, University of São Paulo
conflicts_of_interest: Some authors reported personal fees/DSMB roles with industry (e.g., Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, J&J, Merck, AstraZeneca); no other conflicts reported for the remaining authors
extraction_notes: Trial registered NCT04523064. AKI adjudicated blinded to treatment; secondary outcomes not adjudicated.
overall_extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes included AF and type 5 MI (not prespecified in this project). Length of stay was not directly reported as mean/SD; only hospital-free days were provided, so no LOS data extracted.

title: Evaluation of the effect of empagliflozin on prevention of atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
authors: Zarei B; Fazli B; Tayyebi M; Abbasi Teshnizi M; Moeinipour A; Javedanfar O; Javidi Dasht Bayaz R; Rahmati M; Ghavami V; Amini S; Mohammadpour AH
study_design: Double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial
setting: Single-center tertiary academic hospital (Mashhad University of Medical Sciences) for elective off-pump CABG
analysis_population: Adults aged 18–70 years undergoing elective off-pump CABG, on background guideline-directed medications
surgery_or_procedure: Coronary artery bypass grafting (off-pump)
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily starting 3 days before surgery and continued through the first 3 postoperative days (total 6 days) in addition to standard care
exposure_timing: Initiated preoperatively (3 days before CABG) and continued perioperatively to postoperative day 3
follow_up: Primary monitoring for arrhythmias during the first 72 h after surgery; other labs and parameters reported up to postoperative day 3; discharge outcomes not clearly reported
extraction_notes: The trial primarily evaluated postoperative arrhythmias and CRP. Prespecified outcomes for this project (AKI, mortality, HF, MACE, euglycemic DKA, hospital length of stay) were not explicitly reported with extractable data in the available PDF.
overall_extraction_notes: No explicit data found for the prespecified outcomes: postoperative AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, major adverse cardiovascular events, euglycemic DKA, or length of hospital stay. The manuscript focuses on arrhythmia outcomes, ECG/echo parameters, CRP, and short-term hemodynamic/lab measures within 72 h to postoperative day 3.

title: The effects of sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibition on cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: An open-label randomized pilot study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Rampanelli E; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
study_design: Prospective, single-center, open-label, phase IV, randomized, parallel-group controlled pilot trial (1:1). Intention-to-treat analysis.
setting: Tertiary academic hospital (Amsterdam UMC); adult elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily from three days before surgery until postoperative day two.
exposure_timing: Started 3 days preoperatively; continued through postoperative day 2.
follow_up: Biomarkers on POD1 and POD2; AKI incidence within 7 days post-surgery; intraoperative ketones; in-hospital complications.
funding: European Union Horizon 2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No. 101024833.
conflicts_of_interest: One author (DHR) reported consulting and research funding from multiple pharmaceutical companies; all honoraria paid to employer. Other authors declared no conflicts.
extraction_notes: Trial was stopped early at ~75% enrollment due to observed AKI difference. Supplementary tables with detailed complications not available in provided text.
overall_extraction_notes: Mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, postoperative heart failure, and total hospital length of stay were not extractable from the provided text (reported only as part of supplementary material or not reported).

title: Initiation of peri-operative SGLT2 inhibitor reduces mortality and cardiovascular events after surgical aortic valve replacement
authors: Yan, J.; McKinnerney, J.; Al Janabi, T.; Korgaonkar, N.; Kashyap, R.
study_design: Retrospective multicenter cohort study with 1:1 propensity score matching using electronic health records
setting: TriNetX Research Network (multi-institutional EHR database across U.S. healthcare organizations)
analysis_population: Adults (≥18 years) undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR); exposure defined as preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor use initiated 30 to 3 days prior to SAVR; matched to non-users with no prior SGLT2i use
total_sample_size: 880 (after matching: 440 pre-op SGLT2i users; 440 matched non-users)
surgery_or_procedure: Surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR)
intervention_or_exposure: Initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy preoperatively
comparator: Matched non-users of SGLT2 inhibitors (no prior SGLT2i)
funding: Authors reported no specific funding for this study.
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes were 1-year all-cause mortality and MACE; safety outcomes included AKI and UTI. Only prespecified outcomes from the review protocol were extracted here.
overall_extraction_notes: All data extracted from the full-text PDF. The study reports 1-year all-cause mortality (not prespecified as in-hospital mortality) and does not report euglycemic DKA or length of hospital stay; therefore these outcomes are not extracted here.

title: Evaluation of the effect of empagliflozin on prevention of atrial fibrillation after heart valve surgery: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.
authors: YazdFazeli M; Samimi S; Abbasi Teshnizi M; Hoseinikhah H; Moeinipour A; Javedanfar O; Ghavami V; Abedi F; Amini S; Fazli B; Mohammadpour AH
journal: Indian journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
study_design: Single-center, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial (mITT primary analysis)
setting: Imam Reza Hospital, Mashhad University of Medical Sciences; adult elective heart valve surgery with CPB
analysis_population: mITT population: randomized patients with at least one assessable primary outcome; 40 empagliflozin vs 41 placebo
surgery_or_procedure: Elective heart valve surgery (MVR, AVR, TVR, PVR; some with concomitant CABG) under general anesthesia with cardiopulmonary bypass
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily
exposure_timing: Initiated 3 days preoperatively and continued through postoperative day 3 (total six doses)
comparator: Matching placebo on the same schedule plus standard care
follow_up: Postoperative continuous ECG monitoring for 72 h; daily in-hospital clinical/lab safety monitoring; hospital length of stay recorded to discharge
funding: Research Council of Mashhad University of Medical Sciences
overall_extraction_notes: Primary outcome of the trial was POAF (not a prespecified outcome for this review). No explicit reporting of acute kidney injury, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, or MACE. eDKA explicitly reported as zero events in both groups. Length of hospital stay presented as medians with IQR only.

title: Dapagliflozin and Acute Kidney Injury Following Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Hulst AH; de Oliveira NPM; Niesten ED; Wietsma NE; Gerritse BM; Scohy TV; Rettig TCD; Snellen FTF; Voogd MF; Godfried MB; de Boer RN; Wink J; van der Werff LMM; Cobbaert CM; Ruhaak LR; Eberl S; Preckel B; Hollmann MW; Schenk J; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; MERCURI-2 Study Group
study_design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial (RCT).
setting: Seven hospitals (2 academic, 5 nonacademic). Adult elective cardiac surgery patients.
analysis_population: Intention-to-treat for primary outcome (392 vs 392). Per-protocol exploratory analysis included patients who took all 4 doses.
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiac surgery including CABG, valve repair/replacement, and aortic root/arch procedures; majority with cardiopulmonary bypass.
intervention_or_exposure: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily, 4 total doses: evening before surgery, morning of surgery, postoperative day 1, and postoperative day 2.
exposure_timing: Initiated 1 day prior to surgery and continued through postoperative day 2 (4 doses).
comparator: Matching placebo administered on the same schedule.
follow_up: Primary outcome assessed within 7 postoperative days; secondary outcomes (e.g., MACE) at 30 days; postoperative adverse events during the postoperative period.
funding: Supported by The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development (ZonMw, grant 10140022010003). Additional investigator funding from EU Horizon 2020 (Marie Skłodowska-Curie 101024833), ESAIC/BJA Charity, ZonMw (Veni-09150162410006), Dutch Diabetes Foundation, and Dutch Kidney Foundation.
conflicts_of_interest: Reported: grants/fees outside the submitted work for multiple authors. Examples: funding from Roche Diagnostics (Rettig), ESAIC/ZonMw (Preckel), editorial roles (Hollmann), grants/advisory boards with AstraZeneca, Boehringer Ingelheim, Eli Lilly, MSD, Novo Nordisk, Sidero Bio (van Raalte). Others reported no disclosures.
overall_extraction_notes: No explicit data for in-hospital mortality or euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis were reported. Ketoacidosis was listed as a safety event (1 vs 0) without specifying euglycemic status, so it was not extracted under the EDKA outcome.

title: Differential Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and SGLT2 Inhibitor Add-on Therapy on Outcomes Following Cardiac Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authors: Biswas S; Wahba A; Srivastava Y; Kumar K; Chintagumpala V; Said SM
study_design: Propensity score-matched analysis
surgery_or_procedure: Cardiac surgery
intervention_or_exposure: SGLT2 inhibitor add-on therapy; GLP-1 receptor agonist add-on therapy
comparator: GLP-1 receptor agonist add-on therapy (per title; comparator to SGLT2 inhibitor add-on therapy)
extraction_notes: Only bibliographic metadata (title/authors/journal) available; no abstract or full text provided. Study appears to compare outcomes after cardiac surgery between GLP-1 RA and SGLT2 inhibitor add-on therapies using propensity score matching.
overall_extraction_notes: No abstract/full text available in provided materials. Unable to extract sample sizes, group details, or any prespecified outcomes (AKI, mortality, HF, MACE, EDKA, LOS). Study design and interventions inferred solely from the title.

title: SGLT2 Inhibition as a Perioperative Cardiorenal Stabilizer in Cardiac Surgery: Integrated Clinical Cohort and Pleiotropic Network-Based Pharmacological Analysis.
authors: Onar LC; Guner E; Yilmaz I
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort study
analysis_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing open-heart cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass
surgery_or_procedure: Coronary artery bypass grafting, valve surgery, or combined procedures via median sternotomy
intervention_or_exposure: Chronic SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (empagliflozin/dapagliflozin and others) verified by records; ≥90 days of use preoperatively; routinely stopped ~48 h pre-op and generally reinitiated after discharge
exposure_timing: Chronic preoperative use; perioperative discontinuation (~48 h pre-op); mean time to postoperative reinitiation 7 ± 1.6 days; modeled as time-dependent exposure
comparator: No SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (managed with insulin and/or other oral antidiabetic agents)
follow_up: 12 months after discharge from index cardiac surgery hospitalization
funding: This research received no external funding.
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare no conflicts of interest.
extraction_notes: The study’s primary outcomes were rehospitalization time-to-first and recurrent rehospitalization burden. Prespecified outcomes for this review (AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure as an index event, MACE, euglycemic DKA, and length of hospital stay) were not reported in an extractable form.
overall_extraction_notes: Full text reviewed. Study focuses on 12-month rehospitalization outcomes with IPTW and time-dependent modeling. No explicit data for the review’s prespecified outcomes (postoperative AKI during index stay, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure as index event, MACE, euglycemic DKA, or length of hospital stay). Table 2 reports causes among rehospitalized patients only (denominators n=70 and n=102), which are not analysis-ready for the prespecified outcomes.

title: Preoperative Exposure to Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors and Acute Kidney Injury After Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study With Overlap Weighting Propensity Score Analysis.
authors: Ruste M; Vieira A; Le Guennec-Lux Y; Berthod C; Pozzi M; Mewton N; Fellahi JL; Jacquet-Lagrèze M
study_design: Single-centre retrospective cohort with overlap-weighted propensity score causal analysis
setting: Cardiovascular and thoracic centre of a teaching hospital (Hôpital Louis Pradel, Hospices Civils de Lyon)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and with ≥1 indication for long-term SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (T2D with high CV risk, LVEF <50%, or CKD with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Exclusions included eGFR <20, type 1 diabetes, preop AKI, transplant/LT-MCS, preop cardiogenic shock, death before POD1, and CKD conditions without SGLT2i indication.
surgery_or_procedure: Cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative long-term SGLT2 inhibitor medication recorded on preoperative prescriptions; discontinuation defined as withdrawal ≥3 days before surgery per ESC guidance
exposure_timing: Preoperative exposure (with variable continuation or discontinuation before surgery)
follow_up: AKI assessed within 7 days post-surgery by KDIGO creatinine criteria; other outcomes during index hospitalization/ICU stay
funding: No specific grant from public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors
conflicts_of_interest: Authors report no conflicts of interest.
extraction_notes: Propensity score model variables: LVEF category, chronic arterial hypertension, COPD, BMI, preop hemoglobin, preop serum creatinine, loop diuretic, renin–angiotensin system inhibitors, surgery type, and simplified prediction index for RRT. Overlap weighting used for causal relative risks.
overall_extraction_notes: Primary outcomes on AKI were primarily reported as overlap-weighted causal relative risks; raw counts before weighting are also tabulated. ICU length of stay was reported, but total hospital length of stay was not reported; postoperative heart failure and MACE were not reported.

title: Perioperative dapagliflozin in diabetic patients undergoing cardiac surgery: the DAPA-CS trial.
authors: Li Z; Chen R; Han J; Zhou H; Zeng Z; Zhao Y; Liu S; Zhang H; Zheng Z
study_design: Randomized, open-label, blinded-endpoint trial (mITT analysis)
setting: Single-centre tertiary cardiac surgery hospital (Fuwai Hospital, Beijing)
analysis_population: Modified intention-to-treat: randomized patients who underwent surgery; 164 analyzed (81 dapagliflozin, 83 control)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective on-pump cardiac surgery (predominantly isolated on-pump CABG)
intervention_or_exposure: Dapagliflozin 10 mg/day plus standard care
exposure_timing: Administered for at least 3 days preoperatively; withheld on day of surgery; resumed postoperatively once oral intake was re-established through POD 5
follow_up: Perioperative biomarker endpoints through 120 h post-op; clinical events assessed at 30 days and 12 months
funding: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (2021-I2M-1-063); Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases–National Science and Technology Major Project (2024ZD0521904); National High-Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding (2023-GSP-GG-20, 2022-GSP-GG-28); National Clinical Research Center for Cardiovascular Diseases (NCRC2020004)
conflicts_of_interest: Authors report no disclosures of interest
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint was myocardial injury (hs-cTnI), not part of the prespecified outcomes for this review. AKI was a key secondary endpoint. Safety outcomes included DKA. MACE at 30 days and 12 months were reported narratively without extractable counts in the provided material.
overall_extraction_notes: Data for several prespecified outcomes (in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE counts, and length of hospital stay) were not explicitly reported or extractable from the provided figures/text. Only AKI (reported-effect) and DKA (zero events) could be reliably extracted.

title: Enhanced recovery mitigates sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors associated mobility decline in valve surgery patients.
authors: Xu C; Chen M; Lu E; Zhang X; You H; Zhao X; Sun Y; Xu X
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort study
setting: Department of Cardiovascular Surgery, Zhongshan Hospital Affiliated to Xiamen University; ERAS protocol for elective valve surgery
analysis_population: Adults 18–75 years with valvular heart disease undergoing elective valve surgery within ERAS pathway; NYHA I–III; no major extracardiac organ dysfunction
surgery_or_procedure: Elective valve surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass within ERAS program
intervention_or_exposure: Quadruple heart failure therapy including an SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin 10 mg/day or empagliflozin 10 mg/day)
exposure_timing: SGLT2 inhibitor typically continued until the day before surgery; resumed when patients regained ability to swallow after anesthesia recovery
comparator: Triple therapy without an SGLT2 inhibitor
follow_up: Perioperative in-hospital course; assessments at admission, PACU discharge, ICU discharge, transfer to secondary care ward, and final hospital discharge
funding: Authors stated no external financial support for the work/publication
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declared no commercial or financial relationships (none declared)
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes were mobility-related scales and ERAS metrics. The paper did not report prespecified outcomes for this review (AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA). Overall hospital length of stay by group was not reported; only ICU duration and mobilization times were provided.
overall_extraction_notes: Full-text reviewed. Study focuses on perioperative mobility and ERAS metrics in valve surgery patients with or without SGLT2i. None of the prespecified outcomes for this project (AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA, length of hospital stay) were explicitly reported with extractable, group-wise data. ICU duration and mobilization times were provided but are not among the prespecified outcomes.

title: Effects of dapagliflozin on main pulmonary artery diameter in patients undergoing mitral valve replacement: a retrospective observational study.
authors: Wang D; Liu P; Chen X; Hu H; Wang H; Zhang Z; Liu X
study_design: Single-center retrospective observational study
setting: Department of Cardiac Surgery, Affiliated Hospital of Qingdao University; single-center
analysis_population: Adults (≥18 years) undergoing mitral valve replacement for mitral regurgitation with baseline LVEF < 50%, with pre- and postoperative echocardiographic assessment
surgery_or_procedure: Mitral valve replacement (MVR)
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily as part of standardized heart failure management
exposure_timing: At least 2 weeks before surgery (median 4 weeks)
follow_up: Postoperative echocardiography performed at a scheduled follow-up visit approximately one week after hospital discharge
funding: Authors stated no financial support was received for this work/publication
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declared no commercial or financial relationships constituting a potential conflict of interest
extraction_notes: Primary study outcomes were echocardiographic and biomarker percentage changes; prespecified SR outcomes (AKI, mortality, HF events, MACE, euglycemic DKA, length of stay) were not reported.
overall_extraction_notes: The article focuses on perioperative changes in echocardiographic parameters (e.g., MPA diameter) with preoperative dapagliflozin use. None of the systematic review’s prespecified outcomes (postoperative AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure events, MACE, euglycemic DKA, or length of hospital stay) were reported in the text, tables, or figures. Source locations reviewed: Methods, Results, Table 1, Table 2, Figures 1–2.

title: Impact of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Acute Kidney Injury Post Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Retrospective Cohort Study and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Zhou X; Pan Y; Hua K; Yang X
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with 1:3 propensity score matching
setting: Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Department of Cardiovascular Surgery (tertiary academic center)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) meeting inclusion/exclusion criteria; comparison of preoperative dapagliflozin users vs non-users after PSM
surgery_or_procedure: Off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG)
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily (SGLT2 inhibitor)
exposure_timing: Minimum 3 months of uninterrupted therapy preoperatively; stopped 72 hours before surgery
follow_up: AKI assessed within 48 hours after OPCABG; other outcomes assessed during index hospitalization
funding: This research received no external funding.
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
extraction_notes: AKI definition per study: increase in serum creatinine ≥0.3 mg/dL (26.2 µmol/L) or 1.5–2-fold from baseline within 48 hours after OPCABG (Methods).
overall_extraction_notes: Study limited to off-pump CABG population; only dapagliflozin users included in exposure group. No numerical data reported for length of hospital stay, postoperative heart failure, MACE, or euglycemic DKA in the provided text/tables.

title: Preoperative SGLT2i therapy and acute kidney injury in patients undergoing emergency and urgent coronary artery bypass grafting - A causal inference framework.
authors: Kolland M; Sartori S; Klivinyi C; Schörghuber M; Pannold J; Knez I; Kirsch AH; Schreiber N
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort with causal inference weighting (entropy balancing)
setting: Medical University of Graz, Department of Cardiac Surgery (tertiary academic hospital)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing urgent (<48 h) or emergent (≤12 h) isolated CABG with an indication for SGLT2i (T2DM, HFrEF, or CKD). Exclusions: age <18, missing key labs for AKI definition, postoperative mechanical circulatory support, preoperative KRT, reoperation within 72 h, preoperative sepsis/septic shock.
surgery_or_procedure: Urgent or emergent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin)
exposure_timing: Documented SGLT2i use within 2 weeks prior to surgery
comparator: No preoperative SGLT2i use (within 2 weeks prior to surgery)
follow_up: AKI assessed up to 7 days post-op; ICU length of stay during index hospitalization; 30-day all-cause mortality; postoperative diabetic ketoacidosis assessed days 1–7.
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declared no known competing interests.
overall_extraction_notes: Study limited to urgent/emergent isolated CABG. AKI defined solely by creatinine-based KDIGO criteria; urine output not used. Mortality reported at 30 days (not strictly in-hospital); definition preserved in outcome_definition.

title: Postoperative Ketoacidosis in Cardiac Surgery: Incidence, Analytical Profile, and Association With Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors-A Prospective Observational Study.
authors: Ginestal-Calvo J; Flordelís-Lasierra JL; Pérez-Vela JL; Campos-Bermejo L; Coso-Garrido C; Blanco-Carrasco L; Galiano-Carrilero C; Domínguez-Aguado H; Renes-Carreño E
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
study_design: Prospective observational cohort study
setting: Cardiac intensive care unit of a tertiary academic hospital (Hospital Universitario 12 de Octubre), Madrid
analysis_population: Adult patients undergoing elective cardiac surgery; excluded emergency surgery and those without informed consent
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiac surgery (valvular, coronary artery bypass grafting, aortic, or combined procedures)
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative/perioperative exposure to SGLT2 inhibitors (chronic outpatient therapy)
exposure_timing: SGLT2 inhibitors continued until hospital admission the day before surgery; then withheld during hospitalization. Last outpatient dose typically 12–24 hours before surgery.
follow_up: Perioperative postoperative sampling at ICU admission (postop hour 0), hour 6, and hour 16; in-hospital outcomes also collected
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declare no known competing interests.
extraction_notes: Counts for ketoacidosis by SGLT2 exposure are explicitly reported in the abstract (17/28 vs 8/79). Some internal inconsistencies exist elsewhere in the text/tables; abstract figures were used for the dichotomous incidence, and reported-effect estimates were taken as stated.
overall_extraction_notes: The study does not report AKI, heart failure, MACE, or hospital length of stay by SGLT2 exposure. In-hospital mortality and ICU stay are presented by presence of ketoacidosis, not by SGLT2 exposure. Ketoacidosis definition is broader than strict euglycemic DKA; authors state episodes were frequently euglycemic.

title: Impact of SGLT2 Inhibitor Therapy on Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery.
authors: Taghiyev ZT; Beier LM; Leweling C; Gunkel S; Sadowski KM; Assmus B; Boening A
surgery_or_procedure: Cardiac surgery
intervention_or_exposure: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy
extraction_notes: Only bibliographic metadata available via PubMed; full text PDF not available. No extractable numerical outcomes without the full text/abstract details.
overall_extraction_notes: Insufficient data for quantitative extraction. The title indicates evaluation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy in patients undergoing cardiac surgery, but study design, sample size, groups, and outcome results are not available from metadata alone.

title: Retrospective Chart Review of Euglycemic Diabetic Ketoacidosis Rates and Outcomes Postimplementation of Sodium Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use Stoppage 5 Days Before Open Heart Surgery.
authors: Auerbach JS; Alnajar A; Patel SS; Gershengorn HB; Lamelas J; Perez D; Aljure OD; Ferreira TD; Gonzalez LA; Cabrera JL
journal: Journal of cardiothoracic and vascular anesthesia
study_design: Retrospective cohort (chart review) with propensity score–matched analysis
analysis_population: Adults undergoing open heart surgery within 24 hours of hospital admission; compared patients prescribed SGLT2 inhibitors preoperatively (instructed to stop 5 days before surgery) versus patients not on SGLT2 inhibitors.
